problem: Modular mobile-manipulation pipelines suffer hand-off errors between skills and rely on a fixed, non-reactive task plan, while monolithic end-to-end policies (RL or Decision Transformer) fail on long-horizon multi-skill tasks with egocentric vision.
motivation: Home rearrangement needs both accurate whole-body low-level control and high-level decisions (e.g. open a closed drawer first, retry if it fails). Prior Habitat rearrangement methods use a fixed skill order and cannot adapt to closed receptacles or disturbances. The paper aims to keep skill modularity while learning a single policy end-to-end.
key_idea: A causal-transformer policy that first infers the active skill ID (supervised by skill labels from a modular expert) and then predicts whole-body low-level actions conditioned on that skill embedding, trained end-to-end by imitation.
insight: Explicitly conditioning action prediction on an inferred skill works much better than using skill prediction as an auxiliary loss: DT (Skill) reaches only 7.67% vs ST 19.17% on unseen scenes, and removing the skill inference module or replacing the transformer with an LSTM sharply lowers success. Because the skill is re-inferred every step, the policy re-opens a drawer that was snapped shut (19.5% pick success under perturbation vs 0.5% for M3 Oracle) even though it never saw perturbations in training. Moderate context (30) beats 15 or 60.
method: Input encoding: 256x256 depth goes through ResNet-18 (256-d) and proprioception (joint angles, holding flag) plus object/goal coordinates go through an MLP (256-d); they are concatenated into a 512-d token with a time positional embedding, over context C=30.

Skill Inference module: 2-layer causal transformer (hidden 512) that outputs a one-hot skill (navigate, pick, place, open drawer, open fridge) per step, embedded as z_t. Trained with focal loss to handle class imbalance.

Action Inference module: a causal transformer over interleaved tokens (x_t, a_{t-1}, z_t), 90 tokens for C=30, that outputs a 12-d action: 7 arm delta-joint means (Gaussian), 2 base velocity means (Gaussian), 3 gripper logits (open/close/keep). Trained with MSE + focal loss.
Teacher forcing: ground-truth skill labels are fed to the action module in training and inferred skills at test time, so both modules train in parallel.
Auxiliary head: predicts which receptacle contains the target object (M+1-way CE) using privileged simulator info, used only in training, to teach the policy when to open which receptacle.

Demonstration data: 10k demos generated by M3 skills (RL-trained) plus an oracle task planner, with skill labels per step. Rearrange-Hard training is fine-tuned from a policy pretrained on easy-split episodes.
Total policy size is 16M parameters (2M for the transformer in the skill module).

setting.backbone: ResNet-18 + 2-layer causal transformers (Skill Inference + Action Inference), trained from scratch by imitation
setting.training_data: 10,000 demonstrations from the M3 (Oracle) data-generating policy on Habitat Rearrangement Challenge train episodes (50k configurations, 63 scenes); easy-split pretraining plus Rearrange-Hard fine-tuning
setting.observation: egocentric 256x256 depth (head camera), joint angles, holding flag, base egomotion, plus given 3D start object and goal positions
setting.action_space: continuous whole-body: 7 arm delta joint positions (PD control), base linear/angular velocity, 3-way gripper (open/close/keep)
setting.privileged: none at test time (object and goal positions are given by the task; the receptacle indicator and skill labels are used only in training)

numbers.eval_set_note: 400 episodes in 20 unseen scene configurations (100 easy / 200 hard / 100 very hard), a harder re-mix of the Habitat Rearrangement Challenge data
numbers.extra: trained on 10k M3-oracle demos; mean of 3 seeds; 5000-step horizon; 15cm success radius

numbers_note: Rearrange-Hard is the paper's own harder split of the Habitat Rearrangement Challenge, not a canonical benchmark. Ablation results (architecture, context length, dataset size) are given only in figures. The incomplete-demonstration ablation is 36.5% seen and 27.8% unseen on the easy split.
results: ST reaches 19.17% SR on unseen Rearrange-Hard, beating the best non-oracle baseline M3 (13.25%) and DT (Skill) (7.67%). M3 gets 0% on hard and very hard, while ST gets 15.83% and 8.0%. ST also beats M3 (Oracle) on hard and very hard, though M3 (Oracle) is higher overall (22.58%) and on easy. Under drawer-closing perturbation, ST keeps 19.5% pick success vs 0.5% for M3 (Oracle).
limitations: Absolute success rates remain low (~19% overall), and easy-split performance (37%) is below M3's (53%).
Geometric goal specification cannot identify the target object once it shifts inside an opened drawer.
Depends on an RL-trained modular expert with oracle planner and skill labels for demonstrations; simulation only, and no RL fine-tuning.
